The combustion chamber is a cylinder of length 0.2 m and diameter 0.1 m modeled as 2D axisymmetric.
The air co-flow enters at a velocity of U=(10,0,0) m/s, temperature of 800 K, and pressure of 101325 Pa.
The inlet air composition by mass fraction is O2=0.233 and N2=0.767.
The chamber is initially filled with this same air at 800 K and 101325 Pa.
Liquid dodecane is injected through a cone injector positioned at the center of the inlet.
The liquid dodecane mass flow rate is 0.002 kg/s.
The initial droplet velocity is 10 m/s aligned with the axial direction.
The droplet diameter follows a Rosin-Rammler distribution with a mean diameter of 50e-6 m.
The initial droplet temperature is 300 K.
The injection cone angle is 30 degrees total, corresponding to a 15 degree half angle.
The turbulence model is k-epsilon.
The turbulence-chemistry interaction model is EDC.
The combustion chemistry uses a two-step global reaction mechanism for n-dodecane.
The thermodynamic properties of the species are modeled using janaf data.
The simulation is performed with the reactingParcelFoam solver.
